disease_label_per_paper: Extremely severe cellulitis in a lymphedematous lower extremity complicated by septic shock
presentation_summary: 37-year-old man with 10 years of chronic painless right lower-extremity lymphedema was transferred for an extremely severe case of cellulitis.

After three days of cellulitis symptoms, he had intense leg pain, scrotal swelling, fevers, chills, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, delirium, hypotension, tachycardia, respiratory distress, and required intubation and norepinephrine.
On arrival, temperature was 40.1 degC, blood pressure 94/32 mmHg, heart rate 132/min, and oxygen saturation 95% on SIMV.
Exam showed massive edema and erythema of the right leg extending across genitalia and left groin, hot skin, blistering, pustular exudates, verrucae, and nodularity.
Fournier gangrene and necrotizing fasciitis were considered but ruled out; blood cultures had no growth while wound cultures grew mixed organisms.

actual_treatment.source_text_value: transferred intubated and maintained on continuous norepinephrine
antibiotic regimen began with high dose penicillin drip, ciprofloxacin, and clindamycin
regimen changed to fluconazole, metronidazole, and ampicillin/sulbactam
received dialysis on Loyola hospital day 4 and three additional dialysis treatments

outcome.source_text_value: discharged on hospital day 16 with cellulitis resolved, renal function and electrolytes normalized, and ambulating independently

confirmatory_findings.finding: Cellulitis resolved after wound care and antimicrobial therapy

quality_warnings: The rankable evidence preserves shock physiology, lymphedema, massive local cellulitis, and renal injury. Wound culture organisms, negative blood cultures, final exclusion of Fournier gangrene, and treatment response are confirmatory/non-ranking.
